name: Quick weird payoffs
what: Run it, something strange or beautiful happens within a minute. Pictures into sound, bytes into geometry, braille physics, colour chemistry in a pipe.

name: Sound and live coding
what: Make noise, music, or audio structures from the terminal. Sequencers, synths, modem tones, morse, spatial audio, live-coded sound.

name: Take things apart
what: Reverse engineering, binary exploration, watching programs execute, poking at file formats, circuits, firmware, apps.

name: Radio and hardware
what: SDR, ISM-band decoding, USB and HID poking, serial, anything that talks to a physical thing. Often needs hardware, tag it.

name: Fundamentals you never look at twice
what: Protocols and plumbing that run all day in every house and nobody looks at. UPnP, SOAP, mDNS, ARP, DHCP, DNS internals, TLS handshakes. The entry is a door into the protocol, the tool is the key.

name: Deeper rabbit holes
what: Real scientific or mathematical software you can actually run at home. Seismology, particle physics, groundwater, RNA folding, knots, digital evolution. Days-off material.

name: Languages and unusual utilities
what: Esoteric or unusual languages, databases with a twist, old-school environments, one-of-a-kind utilities that fit nowhere else.

name: Games
what: Actual games you play in the terminal. Only the strange or excellent ones.
